question: What is the main goal of quality improvement in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Continuous and structured refinement of care systems
options.B: Increasing the cost of specialized medical treatments
options.C: Reducing the overall number of employed nurses
options.D: Punishing staff members who make medication errors

explanation: You've got this! Quality improvement is all about making systems and care processes better over time, rather than pointing fingers or blaming individuals when mistakes happen. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it so important to involve different specialists (like social workers) when a client has complex psychosocial needs?

options.A: It ensures specialized, long-term support beyond general nursing scope
options.B: It allows the nurse to stop visiting the client's home entirely
options.C: It guarantees that the client's physical illness will be cured
options.D: It replaces the need for family involvement in client care

explanation: Nurses wear many hats, but emotional and financial tangles often need dedicated experts. Bringing in social workers and counselors ensures the client gets the deep-dive help they deserve. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h8)

question: In a busy ward, what do we mean by 'alarm fatigue'?

options.A: The batteries dying in portable monitoring gadgets
options.B: The machine sensors wearing out after long use
options.C: Getting so used to constant beeps that staff start ignoring them
options.D: A power cut that shuts off all bedside monitors

explanation: When too many false or minor alarms go off, nurses can become desensitized. That's why managing alarm settings safely is a vital nursing skill! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the best way to start counselling a mother whose child is experiencing growth faltering?

options.A: Tell the mother to stop coming to the clinic until next year
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about recent feeding and illness
options.C: Scold the mother for failing to feed the child properly
options.D: Write a prescription for expensive imported vitamin supplements

explanation: Great nursing starts with empathy and listening. Ask gentle, open questions to understand what's happening at home without judging. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h8)

question: Around what decade did psychotropic medications like chlorpromazine first become widely available?

options.A: The 1920s
options.B: The 1950s
options.C: The 1800s
options.D: The 1980s

explanation: The 1950s changed everything! The arrival of chlorpromazine and other drugs marked a massive turning point in how mental illness was treated medically. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h5)

question: What does an HbA1c test measure in a patient with diabetes?

options.A: How well the kidneys are filtering waste products from blood
options.B: The exact amount of insulin currently stored in the liver
options.C: Average blood sugar levels over the past three months
options.D: Immediate blood glucose level at the exact time of the test

explanation: HbA1c measures glucose attached to hemoglobin red blood cells, reflecting average control over their lifespan of about three months. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why is it so important to set clear, specific objectives during the planning stage?

options.A: It guides what activities to do and helps measure future success
options.B: It replaces the need to collect baseline data
options.C: It guarantees that no unexpected problems will ever occur
options.D: It ensures that nurses never have to work in rural areas

explanation: Clear objectives act like a map. They show you your daily steps and let you check later whether you actually reached your destination. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the main focus of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after an adverse event?

options.A: Identifying the underlying system failures that allowed the error to happen
options.B: Deciding how much compensation to pay the affected family
options.C: Finding the single individual staff member to blame for the mistake
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of the equipment damaged during the event

explanation: RCA looks beyond human error to uncover weak processes and system gaps that need fixing. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is an essential demographic detail to record in a family planning file?

options.A: Favorite recreational activities
options.B: Client age and residential address
options.C: Detailed family genealogy
options.D: Preferred holiday destinations

explanation: Demographic information includes basic identifying facts like name, age, and address to ensure correct client identification. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h2)

question: Why is reaching a consensus often preferred when working with village health committees on new health programs?

options.A: It ensures local stakeholders genuinely support and accept the program
options.B: It is the fastest possible way to make administrative decisions
options.C: It prevents any member from ever raising a question or concern
options.D: It allows the nurse leader to bypass community opinions entirely

explanation: Consensus means everyone agrees to support the decision, which builds strong community ownership and cooperation. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major complication commonly associated with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: Increased risk of blood clots
options.B: Severe bacterial infections
options.C: Permanent loss of hearing
options.D: High blood cholesterol levels

explanation: Hearing loss is not a standard complication of nephrotic syndrome, whereas clotting risks, infections, and high cholesterol are well-known dangers. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h6)

question: At what exact times after birth is a newborn's Apgar score routinely checked?

options.A: One and five minutes
options.B: Twelve and twenty-four hours
options.C: Ten and twenty minutes
options.D: One and six hours

explanation: Think '1 and 5'! The 1-minute score shows how the baby handled the stress of birth, while the 5-minute score shows how well they are adapting to life outside the womb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h5)

question: What development after World War II greatly boosted the progress of nursing research?

options.A: The creation of graduate master's programs in nursing
options.B: The invention of the electronic medical record
options.C: The complete replacement of doctors by nurse practitioners
options.D: The banning of all traditional hospital routines

explanation: Master's programs gave nurses the formal scientific training required to design, fund, and conduct independent research studies. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h3)

question: A husband accompanies his pregnant wife to antenatal care. What should the nurse encourage him to learn?

options.A: Counsel other couples in the waiting room.
options.B: Learn about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness.
options.C: Perform a physical abdominal examination on his wife.
options.D: Prescribe prenatal vitamins to prevent anemia.

explanation: Teaching partners about warning signs ensures they can act quickly if an emergency happens. Wonderful! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why do we pull an NG tube out in one quick, smooth motion?

options.A: To minimize patient discomfort and reduce gagging
options.B: To ensure the stomach stays permanently inflated
options.C: To make sure the tape stays attached to the nose
options.D: To prevent the tube from breaking into tiny pieces

explanation: Doing it smoothly and quickly gets it over with fast, saving your patient from extra throat irritation and gagging. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T1#GNS212_U1_T1_h8)

question: Why is moist heat therapy so helpful for a patient dealing with chest and airway congestion?

options.A: It expands the lung tissue to increase total capacity
options.B: It loosens thick mucus and soothes irritated airways
options.C: It kills all bacterial infections in the chest instantly
options.D: It cools down body temperature during a high fever

explanation: You got it! Warm moisture works like magic to thin out sticky, thick mucus in the upper airway, making it much easier to cough up while calming down raw, irritated throat linings. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h1)

question: You are getting ready to shock with a manual defibrillator. What is the right sequence right before pressing the discharge button?

options.A: Charge the machine, announce 'clear', and visually check the team
options.B: Pause compressions, check the pulse, and apply gel pads
options.C: Administer emergency epinephrine and remove oxygen tubing
options.D: Turn off the mechanical ventilator and disconnect all IV lines

explanation: Safety first! Always charge the machine, shout a loud 'clear!', and double-check with your eyes that nobody is touching the patient before you hit that button. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you should do as a nurse when a ventilator alarm sounds?

options.A: Check the patient directly and assess circuit connections
options.B: Call the physician immediately to request new settings
options.C: Silence the alarm permanently at the main console
options.D: Increase the oxygen percentage to 100 percent

explanation: Always check the human before the machine! Walk straight to the bedside to make sure the patient is safe and the breathing tube hasn't popped loose. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h4)

question: What happens to calcium levels inside smooth muscle cells when they need to relax?

options.A: Levels fluctuate in a rapid cycle
options.B: Levels decrease
options.C: Levels remain completely unchanged
options.D: Levels increase significantly

explanation: Good job! A drop in calcium stops the muscle fibers from sliding together, allowing the muscle to relax and widen. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason we give packed red blood cells to a patient?

options.A: To replace lost clotting factors
options.B: To boost white blood cell counts
options.C: To improve oxygen-carrying capacity
options.D: To correct low serum albumin levels

explanation: You've got this! Packed red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, which acts like little transport buses carrying oxygen from the lungs to every corner of the body. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is poor human resource management dangerous in a hospital setting?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cost of running the hospital
options.B: It leads to increased nurse burnout and medical errors
options.C: It makes doctors work longer shifts in the surgical ward
options.D: It prevents patients from visiting the outpatient department

explanation: When staffing is poorly managed, nurses get overworked and tired. That fatigue can lead to mistakes, which puts our patients at risk. Good HR keeps everyone safe! [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h1)

question: A low blood pressure warning pops up on your bedside monitor screen. Which computer cycle stage just happened?

options.A: Storage
options.B: Output
options.C: Input
options.D: Collection

explanation: Output is what the computer shows back to you on a screen or printer after it finishes processing the data. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which management function involves guiding, motivating, and overseeing staff during shifts?

options.A: Directing
options.B: Planning
options.C: Controlling
options.D: Organizing

explanation: Directing is your hands-on leadership moment where you guide and encourage your team on the floor. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which color of blood collection tube is normally used for a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Red-top tube
options.B: Lavender-top tube
options.C: Gray-top tube
options.D: Light blue-top tube

explanation: Easy to remember in the ward! Gray-top tubes are your go-to tubes for blood sugar and glucose tolerance tests. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h4)

question: Why do nurses commonly use 70-90% alcohol to wipe down small items like medication vials?

options.A: They leave a long-lasting protective film that repels dust for weeks
options.B: They evaporate quickly and effectively denature microbial proteins
options.C: They destroy all bacterial endospores within two minutes of contact
options.D: They are completely safe to ingest if they accidentally mix with IV fluids

explanation: Alcohol is a ward favorite because it acts fast against germs and dries up quickly without leaving any sticky residue behind. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h4)

question: A family caregiver looks very tired and says they can't sleep because of worry over night medications. What should you do?

options.A: Assess caregiver strain and explore local support or respite options
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately due to unreliable family support
options.C: Advise the patient to manage all nighttime medications alone
options.D: Tell the family member that burnout is simply part of being a caregiver

explanation: You got it! Caregiver fatigue is real. Checking on their well-being and finding support helps keep home care safe and sustainable. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h3)

question: A researcher predicts that a new teaching session will change patient compliance rates. What kind of hypothesis is this?

options.A: Control hypothesis
options.B: Null hypothesis
options.C: Alternative hypothesis
options.D: Sample hypothesis

explanation: The alternative hypothesis is your exciting prediction as a researcher—it says, 'Yes! Our new nursing intervention made a real difference.' [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who forgets to take their daily anticoagulant dose?

options.A: Stop taking the medication for the rest of the week
options.B: Double the next two doses to make up for lost time
options.C: Follow the specific clinic guidelines for missed doses
options.D: Take a double dose immediately to catch up

explanation: Never let a patient guess! Doubling up can cause dangerous bleeding, so they should always check their clinic's missed-dose policy. You nailed it! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h8)

question: A patient with a mild fever and routine vaccination needs visits a nearby facility staffed by community health workers. Which level of care is this?

options.A: Quaternary level of care
options.B: Tertiary level of care
options.C: Secondary level of care
options.D: Primary level of care

explanation: Spot on! Community clinics handling everyday things like immunizations and mild fevers are right at the primary care level. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h1)

question: A patient tells you they pulled a double shift, slept for only two hours, and now feel jittery. What should you suspect?

options.A: Severe sleep deprivation is lowering their seizure threshold
options.B: They are developing a severe bacterial infection
options.C: Their brain has permanently cured itself of epilepsy
options.D: They are experiencing side effects from low blood pressure

explanation: Rest is medicine! When patients don't get enough sleep, their brain's natural defense against seizures drops significantly. Always check on their sleeping habits. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h4)

question: What does 'informed consent' mean when planning a home delivery?

options.A: The doctor signs a paper without telling the mother anything
options.B: The family understands the risks and benefits and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The government forces every woman to give birth at home
options.D: The traditional birth attendant makes all decisions for the family

explanation: Informed consent requires that patients are fully aware of what they are choosing and agree of their own free will. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h8)

question: Your patient cannot lift their hips off the bed to get a bedpan underneath. What is the safest way to help them?

options.A: Raise the head of the bed to the high Fowler position before sliding the pan downward
options.B: Forcefully slide the standard bedpan underneath the patient using maximum pulling force
options.C: Leave the patient without a bedpan until a doctor writes a specific order to lift them
options.D: Roll the patient onto their side, place the bedpan against the buttocks, and roll them back

explanation: Never force equipment under a patient! Rolling them gently onto a properly placed pan protects their delicate skin from friction and painful shearing forces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h2)

question: An older patient keeps losing their balance when standing up from the toilet. What should the nurse suggest first?

options.A: Buying a complex electronic pill dispenser
options.B: Giving them a high-dose stimulant
options.C: Moving their bedroom upstairs
options.D: Installing secure grab bars near the toilet

explanation: Safety first! Grab bars provide immediate, physical support right where they need it during risky moves like standing up. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h5)

question: A 36-week pregnant mum asks why the nurse wants her to identify a blood donor and save transport money. How should the nurse reply?

options.A: These steps ensure quick action if an unexpected emergency like heavy bleeding occurs.
options.B: The hospital requires these items as a deposit before admitting any woman in labor.
options.C: Blood donations are used to test your own blood type one final time.
options.D: It is a legal formality that has no real impact on your actual delivery outcome.

explanation: Having cash and a willing blood donor ready beforehand can literally save a life if heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) happens suddenly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h6)

question: A female patient arrives at the clinic with a fractured wrist and several bruises on her torso. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Confront the accompanying partner aggressively to demand an explanation
options.B: Document the injuries as accidental falls without questioning further
options.C: Provide necessary medical treatment while ensuring a safe, private space to talk
options.D: Discharge the patient quickly before the partner becomes impatient

explanation: Treating immediate physical needs while offering privacy and a supportive atmosphere helps build trust for potential disclosure. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is the main way classic quinoline antimalarial drugs work?

options.A: Binding directly to human liver cell receptors
options.B: Destroying the nervous system of the mosquito vector
options.C: Preventing the detoxification of heme inside the parasite
options.D: Enhancing the production of red blood cells in bone marrow

explanation: Well done! As the parasite digests red blood cells, it releases toxic heme. Quinoline drugs stop the parasite from turning this heme into safe crystals, effectively poisoning it. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main building role of lipids in our bodies?

options.A: Building the outer layer of every cell
options.B: Acting as enzymes to speed up reactions
options.C: Providing quick energy for the brain
options.D: Carrying water-soluble vitamins in the blood

explanation: You've got this! Phospholipids and cholesterol act like tiny bricks that form the protective wall (membrane) around all our cells. Great job! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h1)

question: What is a great nursing strategy to help a patient manage a confusing medication schedule?

options.A: Asking the doctor to change frequent daily doses to a once-daily option
options.B: Instructing the patient to double up doses whenever they feel tired
options.C: Removing reminder alarms so the patient learns independence
options.D: Writing instructions in complex medical terminology for clarity

explanation: Simpler is always better! Cutting down how many times a day a patient must take a pill makes it much easier to remember. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good public health strategy for controlling parasite infections?

options.A: Treating community populations with deworming drugs
options.B: Promoting open-air defecation near water sources
options.C: Ensuring access to safe and clean drinking water
options.D: Improving sanitation infrastructure and sewage systems

explanation: Open-air defecation near water sources actually spreads parasite eggs and worsens outbreaks—definitely a practice we want to stop! You got this. [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h7)

question: Because of where the breathing centers are located in the brain, which vital sign must a nurse monitor most closely in pontine injuries?

options.A: Orthostatic blood pressure changes
options.B: Core body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Peripheral oxygen saturation trends
options.D: Respiratory rate and breathing pattern

explanation: Spot on! Since the pons helps control breathing rhythms, keeping a close eye on your patient's respiratory pattern can save their life. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h6)

question: What usually pushes a struggling endocrine system into a severe crisis like myxedema coma?

options.A: An added physical stressor like an infection or surgery
options.B: Taking a normal scheduled dose of hormone pills
options.C: Eating too much sodium in a single daily meal
options.D: Engaging in light walking exercises in the morning

explanation: When the body is already low on hormones, an extra stressor—like getting sick or having surgery—can completely overwhelm it and trigger a crisis. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h7)

question: What does the term 'orthostatic hypotension' mean?

options.A: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
options.B: Swelling in the lower legs due to poor circulation
options.C: A spike in heart rate after eating heavy meals
options.D: High blood pressure caused by sleeping flat on the back

explanation: When blood vessels are slow to adjust to a new position, standing up too fast can cause a dizzy spell because of a sudden drop in pressure. Good to know for patient safety! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why might you still need to watch a patient with a normal blood pressure for poor circulation?

options.A: Blood pressure is the least important vital sign in critical care
options.B: Blood pressure can remain normal even when tissue perfusion is failing
options.C: Blood pressure monitors are always inaccurate in the ICU setting
options.D: Normal blood pressure guarantees the heart is pumping perfectly

explanation: The body is smart—it can tighten blood vessels to keep numbers looking normal for a while, even when tissues are starving for oxygen. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h5)

question: How does oxygen primarily travel through the bloodstream to body tissues?

options.A: Attached directly to white blood cells
options.B: Floating freely as pure gas bubbles in plasma
options.C: Bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells
options.D: Dissolved completely in blood platelets

explanation: The vast majority of oxygen in the body is carried by binding to the hemoglobin molecules inside red blood cells. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: What type of heat loss happens when a baby is laid directly on a cold, unheated examination table?

options.A: Conduction
options.B: Convection
options.C: Radiation
options.D: Evaporation

explanation: Conduction is heat loss through direct contact—like when a warm baby touches a cold surface. Always remember to use a warm blanket on that table! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h3)

question: Why do nurses need to triage patients when the emergency department is packed?

options.A: Because hospital rules forbid seeing patients in the order they arrive
options.B: Because nurses need extra time to complete paperwork for each case
options.C: Because patient needs are greater than available staff and resources
options.D: Because doctors prefer to treat minor injuries before major trauma

explanation: When too many people arrive at once, triage helps match our limited hospital resources to the patients who need help the absolute most. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h1)

question: What does 'Total Fertility Rate' (TFR) actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of women using modern family planning methods
options.B: The average number of children a woman has during her reproductive years
options.C: The average age of mothers when giving birth to their first child
options.D: The total number of children born in a single hospital annually

explanation: Exactly! TFR estimates the average number of children a woman is expected to have throughout her childbearing years. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h2)

question: Why do deep tissues near the bone often get damaged before the outer skin shows a break?

options.A: Deep muscle and fat layers need oxygen more and are weaker against lack of blood flow than surface skin.
options.B: Bacterial growth starts deep inside the bone marrow.
options.C: Outer skin has a natural defense system that completely blocks pressure.
options.D: Sweat and moisture accumulate underneath the skin layers first.

explanation: Think of deep tissues like hungry muscles near the bone—they need lots of oxygen and give out much faster when blood supply is blocked, even before the outer skin looks broken! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is the main advantage of an EHR over an EMR?

options.A: An EHR is cheaper to install and requires no electricity or computer network
options.B: An EHR is designed to share patient data across multiple different healthcare organizations
options.C: An EHR requires physical paper backup files for every single digital entry
options.D: An EHR can only be accessed by medical doctors and never by nursing staff

explanation: The key benefit of an EHR is interoperability, meaning information flows seamlessly across different hospitals, clinics, and specialists. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why does empowering women often lead to smaller, more planned families?

options.A: Employers legally restrict female workers from starting families
options.B: Women lose their biological capacity to conceive after higher education
options.C: Women gain greater decision-making power over their reproductive health
options.D: Government laws force educated women to have fewer children

explanation: Spot on! When women are empowered, they have a stronger voice in deciding family size and birth spacing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h5)

question: Why is forced marriage considered a violation of human rights?

options.A: It strips away personal autonomy and freedom of choice
options.B: It prevents families from sharing their wealth
options.C: It always involves cross-border international travel
options.D: It violates traditional wedding ceremony laws

explanation: Forcing someone into a marriage removes their basic human right to choose their own life partner and future. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which group of people should be involved during a community health situation analysis?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting local tourist attractions
options.B: International pharmaceutical company sales representatives
options.C: Local stakeholders like traditional leaders and women's groups
options.D: Only doctors from the federal capital city

explanation: True community health relies on involving local leaders and residents who understand their environment and hold social influence. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: When counseling a new mother on her diet, what is an important duty for you as a nurse?

options.A: Forbidding the mother from eating local traditional dishes
options.B: Prescribing strict medical weight-loss medications
options.C: Requiring the mother to purchase expensive foreign supplements
options.D: Debunking harmful food myths that restrict healthy eating

explanation: Many cultural myths try to stop mums from eating nutritious local foods after delivery. As nurses, we gently clear up these misconceptions with kindness and facts! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h8)

question: How should a nurse handle bed sheets that are stained with blood?

options.A: Handle them with minimal agitation and bag them securely
options.B: Wash them by hand in the patient bathroom sink
options.C: Leave them on the floor until housekeeping arrives
options.D: Shake them out thoroughly to remove loose debris

explanation: You nailed it! Shaking dirty linens sends dust and germs flying everywhere. Roll them up gently and bag them safely! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: During an antenatal visit, how can a nurse best check a pregnant woman's nutritional status?

options.A: Give her a printed diet sheet in English without asking about her background
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about her usual daily meals and check her weight trend
options.C: Assume she eats well because she looks healthy on the outside
options.D: Wait until after delivery to discuss what kind of food she ate at home

explanation: Chatting warmly about what she actually eats daily and watching her weight trends helps you spot any nutritional gaps early and support her. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h7)

question: Why is meal timing just as important as food choice for a patient taking insulin?

options.A: Consistent meal timing prevents dangerous mismatches with peak medication action.
options.B: Insulin can only digest food if it is eaten exactly at sunrise.
options.C: Skipping meals causes insulin to turn directly into body fat.
options.D: Late meals make the pancreas stop working permanently.

explanation: When insulin is active in the body without food present, blood sugar can drop to dangerously low levels. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h1)

question: A local health clinic invites village leaders and women's groups to help plan a new malaria campaign. Which PHC principle is this?

options.A: Exclusive medical paternalism
options.B: Community participation
options.C: Tertiary care referral
options.D: Biomedical isolation

explanation: When locals help plan their own health programs, it's true community participation in action. Healthcare works best when people are involved! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the most common mild side effect patients report when taking oral expectorants?

options.A: Nausea and gastrointestinal upset
options.B: Sudden loss of color vision
options.C: Permanent hearing loss in both ears
options.D: Severe high blood pressure spikes

explanation: Spot on. Because these drugs work by slightly irritating the stomach lining, mild tummy upset or nausea can sometimes happen. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h6)

question: When helping a Nigerian patient plan a healthy, balanced local diet, which food combination is best?

options.A: High-fat fried snacks consumed without any protein or vegetable source
options.B: Yam or cassava served with beans, fish, and green leafy vegetable soup
options.C: Strictly white refined sugar dissolved in large quantities of clean water
options.D: Imported processed canned foods supplemented with synthetic energy drinks
