question: About how long is a standard research abstract?

options.A: 50 words
options.B: 1000 words
options.C: 250 words
options.D: 500 words

explanation: An abstract is a quick, bite-sized summary—usually kept around 250 words so busy nurses can read it in a minute! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the most important thing to check on a mother right after she delivers?

options.A: Visual acuity and hearing reflex responses
options.B: Uterine tone and amount of vaginal bleeding
options.C: Serum electrolyte levels and kidney function
options.D: Bowel motility and digestive enzyme output

explanation: Safety first! Checking that the uterus feels firm and watching the bleeding amount helps you catch heavy postpartum bleeding early. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is a key nursing duty right before a patient takes a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Confirming that the patient actually followed the fasting rules
options.B: Giving the patient a small snack to boost energy
options.C: Checking their urine output with a dipstick
options.D: Giving a quick dose of insulin just in case

explanation: Always double-check! Asking 'When was your last meal or drink?' ensures you don't send inaccurate lab samples to the path lab. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h7)

question: A cardiac monitor shows a high heart rate for a patient who is lying quietly in bed. What should you do next?

options.A: Unplug all the chest electrodes to stop the reading
options.B: Quickly give a strong heart medication
options.C: Assume the monitor is broken and turn off the alarm
options.D: Check the patient for pain, fever, or anxiety before reacting

explanation: Tachycardia can happen because of pain, stress, or fever—not just a machine error. Always investigate the clinical cause first. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h7)

question: What actually happens when a mast cell 'degranulates' during an allergy attack?

options.A: Antibodies are slowly manufactured inside the bone marrow
options.B: Inflammatory chemicals are rapidly released into the bloodstream
options.C: White blood cells consume and destroy the foreign trigger
options.D: Red blood cells multiply quickly to fight off the allergen

explanation: Mast cells act like tiny storage bags of histamine. When triggered, they pop open and dump their contents directly into your circulation, causing classic allergy symptoms. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h1)

question: What is the main chemical powder used to make a Plaster of Paris cast?

options.A: Calcium carbonate flakes
options.B: Magnesium sulfate paste
options.C: Calcium sulfate hemihydrate
options.D: Sodium chloride crystals

explanation: Dry Plaster of Paris is made of calcium sulfate hemihydrate. When you mix it with water, it changes into a dihydrate form and hardens! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an active failure in the clinical area?

options.A: Poorly designed infusion pump software installed hospital-wide
options.B: A nurse giving the wrong dose because of misreading a label
options.C: Chronic staff shortages leading to extreme nurse fatigue
options.D: A hospital purchasing confusingly similar medication vials

explanation: You nailed it! Active failures are immediate actions taken right at the frontline of care. Every question you answer makes you a sharper nurse! [learn more](GST319_U5_T6#GST319_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why is it vital for hospitals to offer structured support programs for healthcare providers after adverse events?

options.A: To trick staff into admitting legal guilt so the hospital can fire them easily
options.B: To help clinicians process trauma and prevent long-term burnout or leaving the profession
options.C: To replace the need for conducting an actual Root Cause Analysis
options.D: To distract the public from noticing that a mistake occurred

explanation: Support programs protect staff well-being, helping them recover emotionally and continue providing safe care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h7)

question: A patient starts tensing their muscles and pulls away when you try to examine their shoulder. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong painkiller immediately without a doctor's order
options.B: Document that the patient is uncooperative and end the shift assessment
options.C: Stop, explain what you are doing, and encourage relaxation to reduce guarding
options.D: Hold the arm down firmly and finish the examination quickly

explanation: Tension and protective muscle guarding block accurate assessment of joint movement and strength, so reassuring the patient is vital. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main biological goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To provide permanent physical barriers like thickened skin
options.B: To kill all normal flora bacteria residing in the gut
options.C: To stimulate memory cells without causing severe disease
options.D: To permanently disable the patient's innate immune response

explanation: Vaccines give your immune system a safe rehearsal. They train your adaptive memory cells so you're ready if the real germ ever shows up. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h8)

question: How do standard precautions mainly stop infections from spreading?

options.A: By destroying the infectious agent inside the human body
options.B: By completely eliminating the natural reservoir of pathogens
options.C: By increasing the natural immunity of the susceptible host
options.D: By blocking the mode of transmission and portal of entry

explanation: You got it! Think of gloves and masks as road blockers. They stop germs from traveling from the patient to you, breaking the chain of infection right in the middle. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h1)

question: A hospital quality team wants to know the exact percentage of patients discharged in under four days. Which graph helps find this easiest?

options.A: An ogive
options.B: A stem-and-leaf plot
options.C: A scatter plot
options.D: A pie chart

explanation: Spot on! Ogives shine when we need to find running portions and percentages below or above a specific time frame. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T11#GNS217_U4_T11_h6)

question: Which machine uses high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious items?

options.A: Autoclaving
options.B: Incineration
options.C: Municipal landfilling
options.D: Chemical burial

explanation: An autoclave uses hot, pressurized steam to completely destroy all microorganisms on contaminated equipment before it gets reused or discarded. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for gastric lavage?

options.A: Consuming a small amount of liquid plant fertilizer
options.B: Ingestion of strong corrosive alkali acids
options.C: A mild overdose of over-the-counter paracetamol
options.D: Swallowing a non-toxic household plastic toy

explanation: Corrosive substances severely damage tissue, meaning the mechanical friction of a lavage tube can easily cause an esophageal or gastric perforation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of data interpretation in nursing research?

options.A: To hide negative results from hospital administrators and staff
options.B: To collect as many patient surveys as possible without analysis
options.C: To make sure every research study costs less money to run
options.D: To turn raw research findings into meaningful conclusions for care

explanation: Data interpretation translates raw numbers and notes into clear findings that nurses can use to improve patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is your primary role during an emergency intracardiac injection?

options.A: Performing the needle insertion into the chest wall
options.B: Preparing equipment and monitoring the cardiac rhythm
options.C: Prescribing the correct dosage of emergency drugs
options.D: Documenting the discharge summary for the patient

explanation: Teamwork is key in emergencies! You support the doctor by getting gear ready, timing events, and watching the monitor to see how the patient reacts. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which type of surveillance involves public health workers actively visiting facilities to search for cases?

options.A: Sentinel surveillance
options.B: Active surveillance
options.C: Syndromic surveillance
options.D: Passive surveillance

explanation: Active surveillance means health staff take the initiative to go out and look for cases rather than waiting for reports to come in. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h2)

question: A student practices passing a urinary catheter three times on a dummy before doing it on a real patient. What is this called?

options.A: Intrinsic motivational grading
options.B: Passive cognitive observation
options.C: Pedagogical dependency
options.D: Deliberate practice and skill repetition

explanation: Repeating a skill in a safe practice space builds your muscle memory and boosts your confidence for real clinical work. [learn more](GST321_U8_T2#GST321_U8_T2_h5)

question: A patient is fitted with a vaginal pessary for a uterine prolapse. What key instruction must the nurse include in her discharge teaching?

options.A: Leave the device in place permanently without removal.
options.B: Report any unusual discharge, odor, or discomfort promptly.
options.C: Expect the pessary to cure the prolapse within one week.
options.D: Avoid all physical activity while the device is in place.

explanation: You got it! Pessaries need careful monitoring. Any strange discharge or odor is a red flag that could mean irritation or infection, so the patient must report it right away. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h8)

question: What does it mean when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line on a partograph?

options.A: The baby is ready to be delivered immediately
options.B: Labor is progressing faster than normal limits
options.C: Intervention or timely referral is urgently required
options.D: The mother has entered the fourth stage of labor

explanation: Crossing the action line signals prolonged labor, prompting healthcare workers to take corrective action or transfer the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: Which cells in your body carry MHC Class I molecules on their surface?

options.A: Only mature red blood cells
options.B: Almost all nucleated cells
options.C: Only free-floating antibodies
options.D: Only uninfected skin cells

explanation: Nearly every cell with a nucleus wears MHC Class I proteins like an ID badge to show whether it is healthy or infected from within. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which client situation puts them at the highest danger if a fire breaks out at home?

options.A: Living in a single-story bungalow
options.B: Using a standard landline telephone
options.C: Having pale skin and light-colored hair
options.D: Severe mobility impairments preventing quick movement

explanation: If a patient cannot walk or move on their own, they depend completely on you or others to get them out safely. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T8#GNS324_U6_T8_h3)

question: Why do doctors and nurses usually put a patient on a fluid diet?

options.A: To give the gastrointestinal tract a rest while providing hydration
options.B: To permanently replace normal chewing and digestive functions
options.C: To supply high levels of dietary fiber for bowel regularity
options.D: To rapidly increase body weight in malnourished individuals

explanation: When the tummy needs a break after illness or surgery, fluid diets provide easy hydration without overworking the gut. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h1)

question: Which part of Nigeria generally records lower modern contraceptive prevalence rates?

options.A: Major coastal ports
options.B: Capital city districts
options.C: The Southern zones
options.D: The Northern zones

explanation: National health surveys consistently show differences in mCPR across regions, with the northern zones generally recording lower rates than the southern zones. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h2)

question: A community health nurse wants to start a nutrition program in a rural village. What is the best first step following PHC philosophy?

options.A: Build a modern multi-story hospital in the center of the village
options.B: Consult with local community leaders and residents to identify their actual nutritional priorities
options.C: Import expensive foreign dietary supplements and distribute them immediately
options.D: Report the villagers to local authorities for poor feeding habits

explanation: You got it! Community participation always starts by listening to the people first and letting them help identify their own needs and solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h4)

question: Medical asepsis is also commonly referred to by what name?

options.A: Sterile technique
options.B: Clean technique
options.C: Barrier technique
options.D: Isolate technique

explanation: Medical asepsis is called clean technique because its goal is to reduce the number of germs, not eliminate every single one. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the main job of synovial fluid inside a joint?

options.A: To supply blood vessels directly to the articular cartilage
options.B: To anchor skeletal muscles directly to the bone
options.C: To reduce friction and nourish the cartilage
options.D: To produce white blood cells during an infection

explanation: Spot on! Because cartilage doesn't have its own blood supply, synovial fluid acts like engine oil—bringing nutrients and keeping movements smooth. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h4)

question: A couple already has a healthy 5-year-old child, but has been trying for 3 years to have another baby without success. What do we call this?

options.A: Transient infertility
options.B: Secondary infertility
options.C: Primary infertility
options.D: Absolute infertility

explanation: Brilliant! Secondary infertility simply means struggling to conceive *after* having had at least one prior pregnancy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T19#GNS312_U1_T19_h2)

question: A community health nurse opens a delivery kit and finds a soap bar, a plastic sheet, a cord tie, a razor blade, and a cloth. What is the primary role of the razor blade?

options.A: To open other plastic packaging
options.B: To rupture the amniotic sac
options.C: To clean the mother's skin
options.D: To cut the umbilical cord

explanation: The razor blade serves as the sterile instrument dedicated to cutting the umbilical cord cleanly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is a common reason for iron-deficiency anemia in communities that rely mostly on plant-based foods?

options.A: Excessive consumption of lean red meat products
options.B: Low bioavailability of non-heme iron in plant foods
options.C: A complete lack of carbohydrates in local markets
options.D: Too much calcium blocking all stomach acid

explanation: Correct! Plant-based iron is harder for our bodies to absorb than iron from meat, making anemia more common if diets aren't carefully planned. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h6)

question: What is the main job of an autoclave in treating medical waste?

options.A: Freezing body tissues for long-term storage
options.B: Crushing glass bottles into fine reusable sand
options.C: Sterilizing infectious items using high-pressure steam
options.D: Dissolving expired pharmaceutical tablets in acid

explanation: Correct! Autoclaves use high heat and steam to kill off pathogens before the waste leaves the facility. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h5)

question: What proportion of waste produced in health care settings is generally non-hazardous household-like waste?

options.A: 10 to 25 percent
options.B: 95 to 99 percent
options.C: 75 to 90 percent
options.D: 50 to 60 percent

explanation: The vast majority of hospital trash is ordinary non-hazardous waste, just like normal household rubbish. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: Why do nurse managers need to understand economic appraisals?

options.A: Nurses are required to manage hospital investments personally
options.B: Government policies forbid the purchase of foreign medical tools
options.C: Healthcare resources are limited and require careful distribution
options.D: It eliminates all financial waste in clinical environments

explanation: We never have all the money or supplies we want in the clinic! Because resources are finite, managers use these tools to make sure spending helps the most patients possible. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a key part of long-term recovery support outside the hospital?

options.A: Total isolation from all human contact for the rest of one's life
options.B: Complete denial of employment opportunities until age sixty
options.C: Daily mandatory drug infusions supervised by armed security guards
options.D: Participation in peer support groups and ongoing community aftercare

explanation: Staying connected to a supportive community and peer groups makes a huge difference in maintaining long-term recovery. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is it a bad idea to force disaster survivors to talk about their trauma right away?

options.A: It prevents nurses from administering physical wound care treatments
options.B: It violates basic federal hospital discharge documentation policies
options.C: It can re-traumatize the individual and worsen acute stress reactions
options.D: It automatically invalidates all future psychiatric nursing diagnoses

explanation: Pushing survivors to recount horrors before they are ready can cause deep distress. Let them heal at their own pace! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h7)

question: What are standing orders in primary health care?

options.A: Financial invoices sent to patients after receiving treatment at the facility
options.B: Daily attendance registers signed by clinic staff at the start of a shift
options.C: Verbal instructions given by a physician over the phone during an emergency
options.D: Written guidelines allowing nurses to treat specific conditions without direct doctor approval

explanation: Standing orders are pre-approved written protocols that give healthcare workers the legal backing to initiate specific treatments independently. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h1)

question: What is the standard metric unit for measuring liquid volume in the ward?

options.A: Drop
options.B: Grain
options.C: Pound
options.D: Milliliter

explanation: Liters and milliliters (mL) are our go-to units for measuring liquid medications and IV fluids every day. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h3)

question: What is the best first step if an electrical piece of emergency gear fails to turn on?

options.A: Throw the device out the window
options.B: Abandon resuscitation efforts entirely
options.C: Check the power source and cable connections
options.D: Wait for a biomedical engineer to arrive

explanation: Brilliant! Often, it's just a loose plug or unseated battery that you can fix in seconds. Always check the basics first! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why might a clinic suddenly record a higher incidence of a disease after getting a brand-new testing machine?

options.A: The disease has suddenly stopped spreading entirely
options.B: More mild or early cases are successfully detected
options.C: The total population at risk has decreased to zero
options.D: People have completely stopped visiting health clinics

explanation: Better testing tools simply help us catch infections that used to fly under the radar, making the recorded new cases go up! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h5)

question: A patient cannot wrinkle their forehead or smile evenly on the right side of their face. Which cranial nerve is likely affected?

options.A: Cranial Nerve III
options.B: Cranial Nerve V
options.C: Cranial Nerve VII
options.D: Cranial Nerve XII

explanation: Cranial Nerve VII is the facial nerve! It powers all our facial expressions, so trouble here leads to a drooping or asymmetrical smile. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h5)

question: Which disease outbreak is most feared in overcrowded camps with poor sanitation?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Appendicitis
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Spot on! Where clean water is scarce and waste management is tough, water-borne bacteria like cholera can cause rapid and dangerous outbreaks. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h5)

question: What is the core idea behind deductive reasoning?

options.A: Trusting a senior doctor purely because of their title
options.B: Moving from a general premise down to a specific conclusion
options.C: Accepting traditional habits without asking any questions
options.D: Gathering random facts until a pattern appears by chance

explanation: Deduction takes a known general rule and applies it to a specific situation to figure out what follows. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main way typical antipsychotics work in the brain, causing both their main effects and many side effects?

options.A: Stimulation of GABA receptors in the cortex
options.B: Enhancement of serotonin reuptake
options.C: Strong blockade of dopamine D2 receptors
options.D: Inhibition of monoamine oxidase enzymes

explanation: Typical antipsychotics love to tightly bind and block D2 dopamine receptors. This strong blockade stops the psychosis, but it's also why movement side effects happen. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic example of a primary literature source?

options.A: A dictionary definition of the medical term hypertension
options.B: A systematic review article analyzing the findings of fifty different research papers
options.C: A nursing pharmacology textbook chapter listing common drug side effects
options.D: A research report detailing the exact methods and statistical results of a clinical trial

explanation: You nailed it. A direct research report with its own methods and data is always a primary source. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the main goal of doing a hysterosalpingography test during an infertility workup?

options.A: To count the total number of immature eggs remaining in the ovaries
options.B: To check the thyroid gland for signs of overactivity
options.C: To visualize the uterine cavity and check if fallopian tubes are open
options.D: To measure the exact daily progesterone levels in the blood

explanation: Awesome job! During this test, dye is put through the cervix so x-rays can show if the fluid flows nicely through the tubes. You're building solid practical knowledge! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T21#GNS312_U1_T21_h6)

question: Which period is known to be the trickiest for medication errors and missed care?

options.A: Attending a family gathering on the weekend
options.B: Moving between hospitals, rehab facilities, and home
options.C: Routine visits to the local outdoor market
options.D: Switching from daytime clothes to nightwear

explanation: Correct! Whenever a patient moves from one place of care to another, things easily get mixed up or forgotten. That's why we stay extra alert! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main job of the lower esophageal sphincter?

options.A: To control how fast water leaves the stomach
options.B: To release digestive enzymes into the upper esophagus
options.C: To grind solid food particles into a liquid mixture
options.D: To prevent stomach acid from flowing back into the esophagus

explanation: This sphincter acts like a one-way gate, closing tightly so harsh stomach juices don't splash up and burn your food pipe. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the main difference between clinical fatigue and normal tiredness?

options.A: Clinical fatigue only affects muscle tissue, never the brain.
options.B: Normal tiredness lasts for several weeks without interruption.
options.C: Normal tiredness is caused exclusively by electrolyte imbalances.
options.D: Clinical fatigue does not improve with ordinary rest.

explanation: Great job! Think of it this way: normal tiredness goes away after a good night's sleep. Clinical fatigue hangs around even when you've rested well, making everyday tasks feel like a heavy mountain to climb. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h1)

question: In simple terms, what does cellular hypoxia mean for the body's tissues?

options.A: An excess of sugar circulating in the blood
options.B: A dangerous shortage of oxygen supply
options.C: A sudden increase in total body water volume
options.D: A high concentration of red blood cells

explanation: Hypo means low, and oxia refers to oxygen. It simply means the cells are crying out for the oxygen they need to work! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T3#GNS315_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a good role for nurses in preventing abortion-related health issues?

options.A: Educating local communities on modern family planning
options.B: Advocating for better access to safe reproductive care
options.C: Providing friendly contraceptive counseling in clinics
options.D: Punishing patients who admit to trying self-induced methods

explanation: Nurses never judge or punish patients. Our care must always be professional, kind, and focused on healing. You're going to be an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h7)

question: Which type of longitudinal study follows the exact same specific individuals over time?

options.A: Panel study
options.B: Cross-sectional study
options.C: Pilot study
options.D: Trend study

explanation: Exactly! A panel study keeps track of the exact same set of participants across multiple visits. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why do doctors still check cervical polyps even though they are usually harmless?

options.A: To stop chronic pelvic pain
options.B: To prevent permanent infertility
options.C: To rule out potential malignancy
options.D: To cure underlying bacterial infections

explanation: Even though most polyps are completely harmless, doctors always check them just to be 100% sure there are no hidden cancer cells. Better safe than sorry! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h1)

question: What is the main job of reference apps like Zotero or Mendeley?

options.A: To write entire nursing essays and research papers
options.B: To block websites that contain plagiarized text
options.C: To store sources and automatically generate citations
options.D: To check student assignments for spelling errors only

explanation: Nice one! These tools save you stress by keeping your sources organized and generating citations for you. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T7#GNS217_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the medical term for permanently removing a tracheostomy tube when the patient no longer needs it?

options.A: Extubation
options.B: Decannulation
options.C: Cricothyroidotomy
options.D: Cannulation

explanation: De- means to remove, and cannula is the tube! Decannulation simply means taking the tracheostomy tube out for good because the patient can breathe on their own. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is supportive care so crucial when treating newly emerging infectious diseases?

options.A: Specific targeted medications may not yet exist for new pathogens
options.B: Patients recover much faster without receiving any fluids
options.C: Medications are forbidden in federal isolation treatment centers
options.D: Supportive care permanently changes the genetic code of a virus

explanation: Because new pathogens take time to study, treatments often rely on supporting the body's organs until the immune system fights it off. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the main difference between recording and reporting in the clinic?

options.A: Recording is writing down individual patient care, while reporting is summarizing data for higher health authorities.
options.B: Recording is done by doctors only while reporting is for nurses.
options.C: Recording uses electronic tablets while reporting uses paper only.
options.D: Recording happens once a year and reporting happens daily.

explanation: Think of recording as capturing what you do with one patient in front of you, while reporting is putting all those numbers together to send upstream so the government can plan public health! You've got this. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h1)

question: How does a shortage of nursing staff directly impact patient care in a hospital?

options.A: It reduces patient waiting times in the emergency room.
options.B: It increases staff workloads and raises the risk of burnout and errors.
options.C: It automatically improves the quality of surgical procedures.
options.D: It ensures that every patient gets private room nursing.

explanation: Fewer nurses handling high numbers of patients leads to physical exhaustion, mental burnout, and mistakes that threaten patient safety. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h4)

question: A patient's first rapid test is reactive, but the second confirmatory test is non-reactive. What should you do next?

options.A: Perform a third tie-breaker test or follow national guidelines
options.B: Discharge the client and tell them to return in five years
options.C: Declare the client definitively positive based on the first test
options.D: Immediately start the client on full antiretroviral therapy

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Conflicting results mean you need a tie-breaker test or guidance from national protocols before making treatment choices. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T10#GNS216_U6_T10_h4)

question: Which chemical messenger relaxes blood vessels in the penis to start an erection?

options.A: Nitric oxide
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: When arousal happens, nerve endings release nitric oxide. This is the green light that relaxes the smooth muscles so blood can rush in. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T1#GNS121_U4_T1_h4)

question: How do nurses help make hospitals safer against disasters?

options.A: By funding the construction of new earthquake-proof walls
options.B: By purchasing emergency generators with personal funds
options.C: By writing national environmental zoning policies
options.D: By serving on disaster committees and pointing out safety hazards

explanation: Spot on! Nurses use their daily ward experience to help planners catch and fix safety risks early. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h6)

question: How is 'active' surveillance different from 'passive' surveillance?

options.A: It only applies to non-communicable lifestyle diseases
options.B: Data is analyzed by artificial intelligence instead of human statisticians
options.C: Patients diagnose themselves at home using rapid test kits
options.D: Health workers go out to search for cases instead of waiting for patients to arrive

explanation: Active means taking action! Instead of waiting in the clinic, health workers actively go into communities to find hidden cases during outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h4)

question: As a nurse, what is a major safety risk you must watch out for in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Aspiration due to swallowing difficulties
options.B: Spontaneous regeneration of nerve tissue
options.C: Sudden permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Excessive weight gain from hyperactive metabolism

explanation: Swallowing problems (dysphagia) are very common in late-stage Parkinson's. If food or saliva goes down the 'wrong pipe', it can lead to dangerous chest infections or choking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h6)

question: A clinic notices a sudden influx of new patients moving into the local community. How should this affect their commodity calculations?

options.A: The safety box requirements should be completely ignored.
options.B: The clinic should switch exclusively to glass syringes.
options.C: The waste factor percentage must be reduced to zero.
options.D: The projected target population must be increased.

explanation: An increasing population means more people will need injections, requiring an upward adjustment in commodity estimation. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h3)

question: What is the main goal of an Infant Welfare Clinic?

options.A: Emergency trauma management
options.B: Surgical operations for newborns
options.C: Preventive care and health promotion
options.D: Inpatient hospital admission

explanation: You've got this! These clinics focus on stopping illnesses before they start through check-ups and immunizations, rather than treating severe hospital emergencies. Great job keeping kids healthy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h1)

question: Which chronic medical condition is a leading cause of peripheral neuropathy?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Essential hypertension
options.C: Diabetes mellitus
options.D: Asthma

explanation: Long-term high blood sugar levels commonly damage peripheral nerves, making diabetes the most frequent cause of neuropathy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)

question: A typhoid patient suddenly complains of severe, sharp belly pain and their tummy feels hard to the touch. What emergency does this point to?

options.A: Intestinal perforation
options.B: Renal stone formation
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Splenic rupture

explanation: Correct! A rigid tummy and sudden sharp pain are red flags for a perforated bowel—this needs urgent surgical help right away. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h6)

question: How did early hospital-based training affect how nurses worked alongside doctors?

options.A: It created strict hierarchical traditions with medical officers
options.B: It completely removed the need for clinical supervision
options.C: It focused exclusively on advanced surgical techniques
options.D: It granted immediate university professorships to graduates

explanation: Spot on! The old hospital structures set up a very rigid setup where nurses were strictly subordinate to doctors, which modern training is helping to change. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of therapeutic drug monitoring?

options.A: To confirm that the medication is producing the desired clinical effect
options.B: To test if the patient is secretly selling their prescription
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy department bills the patient correctly
options.D: To prove that the physician chose the cheapest available brand

explanation: We monitor to make sure the drug is actually helping the patient heal and not causing trouble. Spot on! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why do international agreements like the Cairo Programme of Action matter for local Nigerian nursing practice?

options.A: They allow nurses to bypass local hospital rules during emergency obstetric procedures
options.B: They eliminate the need for patient consent in family planning clinics
options.C: They legally require international organizations to fund all local nursing salaries
options.D: They provide a standard framework that governments use to shape national health policies and clinic guidelines

explanation: Big global agreements help shape our national laws and clinic guidelines, which directly guide the safe and effective care you will provide to your patients. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h3)

question: A patient tagged as yellow suddenly starts gasping for air and showing signs of shock. What should you do?

options.A: Ask the patient to walk over to the green area
options.B: Leave the patient in the yellow category because triage tags never change
options.C: Re-tag the patient as red and provide immediate life-saving care
options.D: Move the patient to the black category immediately

explanation: Triage isn't a one-time thing; patient conditions change fast! If someone gets worse, you upgrade their tag right away to get them urgent help. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h2)

question: A nurse is interviewing a 15-year-old girl. What is the most important first step to get an honest sexual history?

options.A: Assure the adolescent of strict confidentiality within legal limits
options.B: Involve school teachers in the private interview session
options.C: Limit the conversation strictly to physical vital signs
options.D: Immediately notify the parents of all discussion details

explanation: Brilliant! Teens will only open up about sensitive topics if they trust that their privacy is safe with you. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which natural hazard displaces thousands of people every year in Nigerian coastal and river areas?

options.A: Tidal tsunamis
options.B: Seasonal flooding
options.C: Volcanic eruptions
options.D: Severe blizzards

explanation: Exactly! Heavy seasonal rains often overflow river banks, causing widespread displacement in many parts of Nigeria. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h2)

question: A woman at home experiences heavy vaginal bleeding shortly after delivering the placenta. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Send a family member to buy oral iron supplements from a local shop
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform immediate uterine massage and administer oxytocin
options.D: Document the estimated blood loss in the register

explanation: Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs stimulate contractions to clamp down open blood vessels and stop the bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: Where should you place defibrillator pads on a patient with an implanted pacemaker?

options.A: Cover the pacemaker site entirely with thick rubber insulation
options.B: Apply the pads to the upper back and neck instead
options.C: Turn the pacemaker off using an external magnet first
options.D: Place the pads at least one inch away from the pacemaker device

explanation: Always keep the pads at least an inch away from metal devices like pacemakers. Placing them right on top can ruin the device and block the shock from reaching the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is the main goal of empowering a local community regarding their health?

options.A: Identify their own problems and plan health interventions
options.B: Act as licensed physicians within community clinics
options.C: Avoid paying local taxes for public infrastructure
options.D: Rely entirely on international donors for financial aid

explanation: Empowerment means giving the people a voice and the tools to fix the health issues that affect them directly. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a double-barreled question in a research instrument?

options.A: A question that has more than ten possible answers
options.B: A question written in two different languages
options.C: A question that is asked twice during an interview
options.D: A question that asks about two different things at once

explanation: Double-barreled questions confuse respondents because they combine multiple ideas into a single query. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h4)

question: What is the medical term for a joint that cannot move at all?

options.A: Amphiarthrosis
options.B: Syndesmosis
options.C: Synarthrosis
options.D: Diarthrosis

explanation: You got it! A 'synarthrosis' is a fixed, immovable joint—just like the sutures in the skull protecting our brain. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h3)

question: What best defines an accident in community health terms?

options.A: A planned medical procedure with complications
options.B: A chronic disease with a slow onset
options.C: An unexpected event causing injury or harm
options.D: An unavoidable natural health disaster

explanation: Accidents are sudden, unexpected events that cause physical harm or damage to individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, a serious memory problem linked to heavy drinking, is caused by a shortage of which nutrient?

options.A: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C)
options.B: Thiamine (Vitamin B1)
options.C: Calcium and magnesium
options.D: Iron and folic acid

explanation: Heavy drinking messes with how the body absorbs nutrients. Lacking Vitamin B1 (thiamine) can lead to severe, lasting brain issues if not caught and treated early. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h4)

question: What is the main reason a nurse performs an eye irrigation?

options.A: To flush out chemicals or foreign bodies from the eye
options.B: To deliver antibiotic eye drops for a bacterial infection
options.C: To permanently dilate the pupil for a detailed eye exam
options.D: To measure the exact intraocular pressure of the globe

explanation: Great job thinking practically! Irrigation uses a steady stream of fluid to wash away dangerous substances or particles before they hurt the eye tissues. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which of these everyday nursing actions is an example of medical asepsis?

options.A: Performing an open surgical operation in the theatre
options.B: Wiping down a bedside table with a disinfectant wipe
options.C: Putting on sterile surgical gloves and a gown
options.D: Inserting a urinary catheter using a sterile kit

explanation: Great job! Medical asepsis is all about clean habits—like wiping down surfaces to cut down on germs. Surgical asepsis is what we save for deep, sterile procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why do we view disaster management as an endless cycle rather than a straight line?

options.A: Because recovery takes the exact same amount of time as mitigation
options.B: Because lessons learned during recovery directly inform future mitigation and preparedness
options.C: Because disasters always happen at the exact same time every year
options.D: Because emergency personnel never stop responding to disasters

explanation: Brilliant! Every time we recover from a disaster, we learn valuable lessons that help us get better prepared for the next one. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why do nurses teach patients to use dental floss along with brushing?

options.A: To scrub the tongue and get rid of white coatings
options.B: To push fluoride paste straight down into the tooth roots
options.C: To polish the flat chewing surfaces of the back molars
options.D: To clean out food and plaque from tight spaces between teeth

explanation: Toothbrush bristles are great, but they can't squeeze into the tight spots between teeth. Flossing finishes the job for a truly clean mouth! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary function of the sensory strip located in the parietal lobe?

options.A: Processing touch, pain, and temperature
options.B: Regulating heartbeat and breathing
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movement
options.D: Interpreting visual images and colors

explanation: The sensory strip receives incoming touch and temperature signals from different parts of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h3)

question: Which process is needed to completely destroy tough bacterial spores on surgical instruments?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: Wiping with clean water
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Standard cleaning

explanation: Only full sterilization methods (like using an autoclave) are powerful enough to wipe out all germs and stubborn bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: A patient in contact isolation feels depressed and refuses to open their door for nursing care. What is your best action as a nurse?

options.A: Remove the isolation sign so family members can crowd into the room
options.B: Threaten to discharge the patient immediately if they do not cooperate with rules
options.C: Acknowledge their feelings, explain the care plan patiently, and spend extra social time with them
options.D: Leave the food tray outside and refuse to enter the room for the rest of the shift

explanation: You've got a true nursing heart! Validating their feelings and showing extra care helps ease their anxiety while keeping safety standards strong. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h6)

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why mothers refuse to bring babies for routine immunization. Which data collection method is best suited for this?

options.A: Measuring the height and weight of newborn babies
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccines in the clinic fridge
options.C: Counting the number of cars passing through the main highway
options.D: Focus group discussions with local nursing mothers

explanation: Focus group discussions allow mothers to openly share their personal beliefs, fears, and cultural concerns regarding immunization. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h4)

question: How does food intoxication differ from a food infection?

options.A: Intoxication only affects the upper respiratory system
options.B: Infection has a much shorter incubation period
options.C: Infection is caused strictly by chemical pollutants
options.D: Intoxication results from pre-formed toxins in the food

explanation: Think of food intoxication as getting sick from poisons that bacteria already made inside the food before you ate it, leading to very fast symptoms! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h1)

question: When a nurse takes up a job in a government or private hospital, what is their legal relationship with the hospital?

options.A: A corporate executive with administrative immunity
options.B: An independent contractor with no hospital ties
options.C: A legal agent who owns the hospital facility
options.D: An employee bound by a contract of service

explanation: When you sign a contract to work in a health institution, you become an employee under a formal work agreement. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h1)

question: In which clinical situation would a doctor most likely use an intraarterial route?

options.A: Administering a routine morning dose of oral antibiotics
options.B: Providing daily maintenance fluids for a stable surgical patient
options.C: Giving an intramuscular vaccination for tetanus prevention
options.D: Delivering targeted chemotherapy directly to a liver tumor

explanation: Spot on! When doctors want to hit a specific trouble spot—like a tumor—with maximum medicine power without flooding the whole body, the intraarterial route is super useful. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T13#GNS125_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the main goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To provide temporary ready-made antibodies that last for one week
options.B: To physically block viruses from entering the body through the skin
options.C: To destroy all normal bacteria living inside the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: To stimulate memory cell production without causing severe disease

explanation: Vaccines introduce safe pieces of a germ so your immune system can build memory cells without you getting sick. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h8)

question: If a factory worker is exposed to loud industrial noise for years, which part of the cochlea usually shows damage first?

options.A: The base near the oval window, which processes high frequencies
options.B: The round window membrane protecting the lower cochlear chamber
options.C: The scala media endolymph ducts located in the middle turn
options.D: The apex near the helicotrema, which processes low frequencies

explanation: The base of the cochlea receives high-frequency sounds first as they enter, making it the most vulnerable spot for noise-induced hearing loss. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is a major reason why mothers in rural areas struggle to attend infant welfare clinics?

options.A: Mandatory fees that exceed hospital costs
options.B: Long distance and lack of transport
options.C: Excessive availability of private doctors
options.D: Strict laws prohibiting clinic visits

explanation: You got it! Living far away with bad transport options makes it really tough for rural mums to travel to a clinic regularly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h7)

question: Which of these expenses is considered an indirect cost in a hospital?

options.A: Electricity used to light the entire hospital building
options.B: Bandages applied to a specific wound on a patient
options.C: The specific medication prescribed for hypertension
options.D: Surgical instruments sterilized for one specific operation

explanation: General electricity benefits everyone in the hospital, so you can't assign it to just one patient chart. That's why it's indirect! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h3)

question: A 32-year-old woman who has always had painless periods suddenly develops severe, worsening cramps during every cycle over the last year. Which condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Primary dysmenorrhoea
options.B: Secondary dysmenorrhoea
options.C: Normal ovulatory pain
options.D: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder

explanation: Onset of severe menstrual pain later in life, especially when it progressively worsens, is a classic sign of secondary dysmenorrhoea. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h3)

question: How do large conferences usually differ from smaller seminars in nursing education?

options.A: Seminars always last for an entire week while conferences last only one hour.
options.B: Seminars focus exclusively on international health policies rather than clinical work.
options.C: Conferences are larger gatherings covering broad trends and offering networking opportunities.
options.D: Conferences are strictly hands-on practical sessions held in small hospital rooms.

explanation: Think of a conference as a big gathering where nurses from all over meet to share big ideas and research, while seminars are smaller, cozy deep-dives into specific topics. [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h3)

question: What is the clear, dome-shaped structure at the very front of the eye that bends incoming light?

options.A: The tough sclera
options.B: The clear cornea
options.C: The pigmented iris
options.D: The sensitive retina

explanation: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye that first meets light and helps bend it toward the back. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h1)

question: In the chain of infection, what is the main job of a reservoir?

options.A: It is the natural habitat where pathogens live and multiply
options.B: It is the medication used to kill harmful bacteria
options.C: It is the immune response created by the host
options.D: It is the physical method by which a pathogen enters the body

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the home base where germs hang out, grow, and multiply before they find a new host to infect. You've got this! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a body-wide (systemic) symptom of puerperal mastitis?

options.A: Clear and painless milk flow
options.B: Local redness and warm skin
options.C: High fever and severe chills
options.D: Generalized body aches

explanation: Mastitis causes painful inflammation and blocked flow—definitely not clear and painless! Spotting this makes you a sharp clinician. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h5)

question: What is a common trap to avoid when designing a conceptual framework?

options.A: Sharing the research design with student nurses
options.B: Writing the framework on a white sheet of paper
options.C: Making the framework too complex and cluttered
options.D: Using too few words in the title of the study

explanation: Don't try to cram every single idea in the universe into one diagram! Keep it clean, simple, and testable. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h8)

question: Which Boolean operator should you use when you want to broaden your search to include synonyms?

options.A: WITH
options.B: NOT
options.C: OR
options.D: AND

explanation: The OR operator tells the database to retrieve documents containing any of the listed terms, which expands your results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the function of the coronary arteries that branch off the ascending aorta?

options.A: Carry blood to the upper brain and scalp
options.B: Drain waste products from the lungs
options.C: Connect the aorta to the pulmonary trunk
options.D: Supply oxygen directly to the heart muscle

explanation: The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the aorta to feed the hardworking muscle tissue of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why is priority setting necessary during community mobilisation?

options.A: Resources are limited, so the community must focus on the most pressing problem
options.B: It stops people from talking during community meetings
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to work on more than two diseases at a time
options.D: The government requires every village to solve exactly one problem per year

explanation: Because time, money, and materials are limited, communities must rank their problems and tackle the most urgent ones first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: Where should you put a heavily soiled bed sheet immediately after removing it from the mattress?

options.A: On the clean bedside chair until you finish the bed
options.B: On the clean floor near the foot of the bed temporarily
options.C: Folded neatly on the overbed table for later sorting
options.D: Directly into a designated laundry hamper or bag

explanation: That's right! Putting dirty linen straight into a hamper stops germs from spreading to the floor, furniture, or your uniform. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is septicemia?

options.A: Presence of multiplying bacteria in the bloodstream
options.B: Inflammation limited to the outer layer of skin
options.C: A localized collection of pus in a single muscle
options.D: Sudden paralysis caused by a damaged nerve

explanation: Septicemia happens when bacteria get past local defenses and start multiplying in the general blood circulation, making the patient very ill all over. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: How do blood-borne pathogens usually spread during unsafe injection practices?

options.A: Consuming food prepared by an infected healthcare worker
options.B: Skin-to-skin contact between nurse and patient
options.C: Inhalation of dried viral particles in hospital air vents
options.D: Direct inoculation of contaminated blood into body tissues

explanation: Unsafe needles bypass our body's defenses and deposit infected blood straight into subcutaneous, intramuscular, or intravenous spaces. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is collaboration with traditional and religious leaders important in community mental health care?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nurses and social workers entirely
options.B: They provide the financial funding for all federal hospital budgets
options.C: They hold significant influence and can help mobilize the community against stigma
options.D: They are legally required to write official psychiatric prescriptions

explanation: Because many community members trust local and religious leaders, their involvement helps change negative attitudes and encourages families to seek help early. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which global body defines nursing as autonomous and collaborative care for people of all ages in all settings?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: International Council of Nurses
options.C: Red Cross International
options.D: World Medical Association

explanation: Spot on! The International Council of Nurses sets the global standard definition that highlights both our independent and teamwork roles in healthcare. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why does poor fetal growth (intrauterine growth restriction) happen more often in teenage mums?

options.A: The young mother's body and the placenta compete for limited nutrients
options.B: Fetal growth is naturally faster when the mother is under eighteen
options.C: Adolescents consume too many synthetic vitamins during gestation
options.D: The amniotic fluid volume increases excessively and crushes the fetus

explanation: Since a teenager is still growing herself, her body uses up nutrients that the baby desperately needs for proper growth. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h4)

question: Which task is a key responsibility of the psychiatric nurse during a referral?

options.A: Diagnosing complex neurological disorders without a doctor
options.B: Buying the client's prescription drugs using personal funds
options.C: Making the final decision on hospital budgetary allocations
options.D: Providing education and preparing documentation for the client and family

explanation: Nurses play a vital role by calming fears, educating the family, and getting all the paperwork ready for a smooth transition. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in any hospital?

options.A: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins
options.C: Changing bed linen every morning
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves for all tasks

explanation: Spot on! Good old-fashioned hand hygiene is your number one weapon against hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: Think of a theoretical framework as the backbone of a nursing study. What is its main job?

options.A: Providing funding for data collection and equipment
options.B: Serving as the structural foundation and guide for the study
options.C: Determining the exact sample size needed for the project
options.D: Writing the final reference list in the correct format

explanation: Spot on! Just like a physical building needs a strong frame to stand, a research study needs a theoretical framework to shape how it is designed and understood. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why is it smart to check that gas is actually flowing out of the cannula prongs before placing them on the patient?

options.A: To measure the exact oxygen percentage in the room air
options.B: To confirm the equipment works and gas is actively delivering
options.C: To clear out any trapped dust from the manufacturing factory
options.D: To warm up the cold gas before it touches the sensitive nasal lining

explanation: A quick check saves a lot of trouble—you want to make sure there isn't a kinked tube or a closed valve blocking air before it reaches your patient. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is a common result of supportive and transformational leadership on a hospital ward?

options.A: More communication breakdowns among health workers
options.B: Higher rates of preventable patient falls
options.C: Increased staff turnover and frequent nurse burnout
options.D: Lower medication errors and higher staff satisfaction

explanation: Supportive leadership builds a safe reporting culture and teamwork, which reduces errors and keeps nurses happy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the true purpose of writing a hospital incident report?

options.A: It is used for quality improvement and learning from system flaws
options.B: It serves as a formal legal tool to discipline negligent nurses
options.C: It is placed permanently in the patient's bedside clinical chart
options.D: It is required by insurance companies to calculate hospital bills

explanation: Incident reports are confidential tools meant to help the hospital figure out what went wrong in the system so safety can be improved for everyone. It's about fixing the system, not witch-hunting! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h7)

question: Why can't you rely solely on looking at a vaccine to know if heat has ruined it?

options.A: Heat damage does not change the physical appearance of the liquid
options.B: Vaccines change color only when exposed to freezing temperatures
options.C: Expired vaccines always look completely normal to the naked eye
options.D: Modern glass vials are coated with special heat-reflective paint

explanation: Most heat-damaged vaccines look totally normal! That's why temperature logs and Vaccine Vial Monitors (VVMs) are our best friends. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h4)

question: Why is the rise of non-communicable diseases changing the daily work of primary health care nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for basic medications in rural clinics
options.B: It means nurses no longer need to worry about immunizing infants against infections
options.C: It allows nurses to stop providing care and refer every patient immediately abroad
options.D: It requires long-term patient education, lifestyle coaching, and chronic disease monitoring

explanation: Chronic conditions like diabetes and hypertension demand ongoing support, lifestyle guidance, and continuous follow-up from nurses. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)

question: A head nurse wants to know if a newly introduced fall-prevention bundle actually decreases patient falls over the next year on the surgical ward. Which action represents applying prospective thinking?

options.A: Implementing the bundle today and tracking fall rates prospectively over the coming year
options.B: Interviewing staff nurses about falls that occurred before they were born
options.C: Asking elderly patients to guess why they might fall in the future
options.D: Looking up incident reports from five years ago to see how many people slipped

explanation: Applying a measure today and observing future outcomes embodies the core methodology of prospective clinical research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: Which symptom is most common in nurses who spend long hours staring at computer screens for charting?

options.A: Numbness in the big toes
options.B: Swelling of the lower legs
options.C: Weakness in the handgrip
options.D: Dry and fatigued eyes

explanation: You got it! When we stare at screens, we tend to blink less, which leaves our eyes feeling dry and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT something a government agency typically does in the food supply chain?

options.A: Managing social safety nets like school feeding programs
options.B: Regulating the import and export of agricultural commodities
options.C: Setting retail prices for every independent restaurant in the country
options.D: Enforcing food safety standards and conducting health inspections

explanation: Governments check food safety and handle imports, but they don't micromanage what individual restaurants charge for a plate of food! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h3)

question: When does the postpartum period officially begin?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: Twenty-four hours after delivery
options.C: When the baby takes its first breath
options.D: At the start of labor

explanation: The postnatal period kicks off right after the third stage of labor when the placenta comes out. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h1)

question: A patient comes to your clinic with severe watery diarrhea and dehydration after drinking untreated stream water. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Severe diarrhea and rapid fluid loss after drinking unsafe water are classic signs of a bacterial infection like cholera. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h4)

question: In public health, what does the term 'herd immunity' mean?

options.A: The body builds resistance to infections through natural dietary intake
options.B: High vaccination rates in a community protect vulnerable unvaccinated people
options.C: White blood cells group together to surround and isolate a foreign microbe
options.D: Animals transmit specific infectious diseases directly to human populations

explanation: Herd immunity is teamwork at a community level! When almost everyone is vaccinated, the disease has nowhere to travel, shielding babies and vulnerable neighbors who can't take vaccines. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why do people stopping heavy alcohol use often experience dangerous symptoms like shaking (tremors) and seizures?

options.A: The brain experiences a rebound effect of hyperexcitability
options.B: The liver fails to filter out toxins quickly enough
options.C: The stomach lining becomes irritated by lack of nutrients
options.D: The muscles lose all stored protein and water

explanation: Brilliant! Since alcohol depresses the brain, taking it away suddenly causes the nervous system to bounce back hard and become dangerously overactive. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the nurse's main job when assessing a patient's diet?

options.A: Designing commercial meal delivery services
options.B: Prescribing strict hospital therapeutic diets
options.C: Collecting and evaluating food intake data
options.D: Purchasing nutritional supplements for wards

explanation: You've got this! Nurses gather information on what patients eat to spot any nutrition risks early and plan the best care possible. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h1)

question: A nurse researcher wants to prove that a new wound care protocol prevents infections better than the old method without relying on messy old records. Which study design should be chosen?

options.A: Prospective design
options.B: Cross-sectional snapshot
options.C: Case-control past analysis
options.D: Retrospective chart review

explanation: A prospective design allows the researcher to implement the protocol today and record infection rates moving forward with high accuracy. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h3)

question: Why is environmental sustainability included as a core goal of food policy?

options.A: To reduce the total volume of crops grown worldwide
options.B: To prevent farmers from ever using modern machinery
options.C: To ensure that agricultural land is turned into housing estates
options.D: To protect soil and water resources for future food production

explanation: Sustainability ensures that farming practices do not ruin the environment, allowing continuous food production over the long term. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)

question: What is the correct way to apply eye ointment to a newborn?

options.A: Rub the ointment vigorously over closed eyelids until fully absorbed
options.B: Place a large drop directly onto the center of the open cornea
options.C: Flush the entire eye with saline before squeezing ointment onto the iris
options.D: Apply a thin ribbon along the lower conjunctival sac from inner to outer canthus

explanation: Gently draw a thin line of the ointment along the lower eyelid pocket, moving from the inside corner to the outside corner. Simple and safe! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h4)

question: What is the main job of capillaries in our blood circulation?

options.A: Exchanging gases and nutrients with body tissues
options.B: Storing extra blood volume during rest
options.C: Carrying blood away from the heart under high pressure
options.D: Preventing blood from flowing backward in the legs

explanation: Capillaries are super tiny vessels with very thin walls. This allows oxygen, food nutrients, and waste to pass easily between your blood and your body tissues! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is getting accurate data so important for evidence-based nursing practice?

options.A: It proves that old nursing theories are always completely wrong
options.B: It ensures clinical decisions are based on reliable facts
options.C: It guarantees that every patient will have a short hospital stay
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to document daily care

explanation: You got it! Accurate data gives us solid, trustworthy evidence to use when deciding the best care plans for our patients at the bedside. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h1)

question: Where does fertilization of the human egg normally happen?

options.A: In the ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.B: Along the lower third of the myometrium
options.C: Directly inside the uterine cavity
options.D: Within the peritoneal cavity of the pelvis

explanation: Spot on! The sperm and egg usually meet in the widest part of the fallopian tube, called the ampulla, before starting their trip to the uterus. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h1)
